missing_duplicates.description: Completeness check: missing cells per column and exact duplicate rows.
insights: 'Precip Type' has 517 missing values (0.536%) - categorical; suggested fix: fill with the mode or an 'Unknown' label.
24 fully duplicated rows (0.025%) - remove with drop_duplicates().

outliers.description: Extreme values flagged with two methods: IQR fences (Q1-1.5*IQR, Q3+1.5*IQR) and Z-score (|z| > 3).
insights: Most outlier-prone feature: 'Pressure (millibars)' (3284 IQR outliers, 3.451%).
No IQR outliers in: ['Wind Bearing (degrees)', 'Visibility (km)'].

noise.description: Is there noise in the data, and how much? Each numeric feature is tested for random fluctuation and isolated spikes (= NOISE) and for stuck sensors and physically impossible readings (= DATA ERRORS), then given a verdict.

method.noise_to_signal: Robust noise sigma (MAD of the 2nd difference / sqrt(6)) divided by the feature's robust spread (MAD-based, immune to bad readings). 0 = perfectly smooth, 1 = pure random noise. Window-free, so the daily and seasonal cycles are NOT counted as noise.
method.snr_db: 10*log10(signal variance / noise variance). Above 20 dB is very clean; below 5 dB is noisy.
method.von_neumann: Mean squared step-to-step change / variance. Near 0 = smooth curve, near 2 = random.
method.spikes: A reading more than 4 robust sigmas AND more than 50% of the feature's spread away from the median of its 4 neighbours, while the neighbours agree with each other (one-point blip, not a real step change).
method.stuck_sensor: At least 24 identical consecutive readings on a continuous feature.
method.out_of_range: Values outside the physically possible range of the quantity. They are excluded from the noise tests (and from outliers, correlation, KDE and monthly analysis) and reported as data errors.

insights: Random noise: YES in 2 of 6 features: ['Wind Speed (km/h)', 'Visibility (km)'].
Data errors: YES in 2 feature(s): ['Visibility (km)', 'Pressure (millibars)'].
Noisiest: 'Wind Speed (km/h)' (noise/signal 0.33); cleanest: 'Pressure (millibars)' (0.02).
'Wind Speed (km/h)': moderate random fluctuation (noise is 33% of the signal's spread).
'Visibility (km)': moderate random fluctuation (noise is 17% of the signal's spread); 2542 isolated spikes (2.635%); stuck at 0 for 193 consecutive readings (probably a sensor outage).
'Pressure (millibars)': 1288 physically impossible values (valid range 850 to 1090).
Clean features (no action needed): ['Temperature (C)', 'Apparent Temperature (C)', 'Humidity'].
'Wind Bearing (degrees)' not tested: circular variable (0 and 360 degrees are the same direction), so linear noise tests are not meaningful.
Recommended cleaning: set impossible/stuck readings to NaN and interpolate over time. The outlier, correlation, KDE and monthly sections already ignore impossible values.
Note: wind speed fluctuates naturally (gusts), so its noise flag is expected - smooth it (rolling median / daily mean) rather than deleting points.

monthly_trends.description: Monthly aggregation of every feature (mean, 10th/90th percentile, std), seasonal averages and month-by-month trend lines across the years.
insights: 'Temperature (C)' averages highest in July (22.97) and lowest in January (0.82).
'Humidity' averages highest in December (0.87) and lowest in August (0.64).
Most variable month for 'Temperature (C)': 2013-04 (std 7.22).
Most variable month for 'Humidity': 2015-08 (std 0.23).

correlation.description: Linear (Pearson) and rank (Spearman) relationships between numeric features, plus how the main variables behave for each weather 'Summary'.
insights: Very strong positive link between 'Temperature (C)' and 'Apparent Temperature (C)' (r = 0.99).
Strong negative link between 'Temperature (C)' and 'Humidity' (r = -0.63).
Strong negative link between 'Apparent Temperature (C)' and 'Humidity' (r = -0.60).
'Temperature (C)' and 'Apparent Temperature (C)' are nearly redundant (|r| >= 0.9) - keep one to avoid multicollinearity in a model.
Almost independent of every other feature: ['Wind Bearing (degrees)'].
Average 'Apparent Temperature (C)' is highest for 'Partly Cloudy' (15.39) and lowest for 'Foggy' (-0.21).
Average 'Humidity' is highest for 'Foggy' (0.95) and lowest for 'Breezy and Partly Cloudy' (0.55).

model_phase.description: Model phase: target class balance, preprocessing with sklearn Pipeline + ColumnTransformer, Random Forest evaluated on a time-based hold-out, and feature importance (impurity and permutation).
insights: Class balance on 'Precip Type': severely imbalanced. 'rain': 85,224 (88.4%), 'snow': 10,712 (11.1%), 'Missing / Not recorded': 517 (0.5%).

Imbalance ratio 7.96:1 - without class weighting a model would be biased towards the majority class, so class_weight='balanced' is used and balanced accuracy / F1 are reported instead of accuracy alone.

Preprocessing: 7 numerical features ['Temperature (C)', 'Apparent Temperature (C)', 'Humidity', 'Wind Speed (km/h)', 'Wind Bearing (degrees)', 'Visibility (km)', 'Pressure (millibars)'] and 1 categorical feature(s) ['Summary']; ColumnTransformer = numerical Pipeline (median imputation + StandardScaler) + categorical Pipeline (most-frequent imputation + OneHotEncoder). Impossible readings (1288 cells) are treated as missing, not as real values.
Hold-out evaluation (2014-03-22 to 2016-12-31): accuracy 1.000 (always predicting the majority class gives 0.938), balanced accuracy 1.000, macro F1 1.000.
Near-perfect score: check that no feature gives away the target (data leakage).
Permutation importance (drop in balanced accuracy when a feature is shuffled on the test period): 'Temperature (C)' 50.3 pts, then 'Apparent Temperature (C)' 0.0 pts.
Impurity importance (Random Forest splits): 'Temperature (C)' 51.6%, 'Apparent Temperature (C)' 30.0%.
'Temperature (C)' and 'Apparent Temperature (C)' are almost the same signal (r = 0.99): impurity importance splits the credit between them, so read them together.

interpretation.description: Interpretation of the weather EDA results and the concrete actions to apply: what to fix, what to mask, what to keep for modelling, and which checks are already active in the Pipeline.
interpretation.summary: 96,453 hourly observations across 12 columns (7 numeric, 3 categorical). 517 missing cell(s), concentrated in 'Precip Type' (517 rows, 0.536%). 24 exact duplicate row(s) (0.025%). Constant column(s) with no information: Loud Cover.
findings: 96,453 hourly observations across 12 columns (7 numeric, 3 categorical).
517 missing cell(s), concentrated in 'Precip Type' (517 rows, 0.536%).
Constant column(s) with no information: Loud Cover.
1,288 physically impossible reading(s) were masked as missing ('Pressure (millibars)' 1,288).
2/6 tested feature(s) show noise (mean noise-to-signal 0.122); error-like features: Visibility (km), Pressure (millibars).
6,424 IQR outlier reading(s) across 7 feature(s), most in 'Pressure (millibars)' 3,284 (3.451%).
Predictive check: accuracy 1.000, balanced accuracy 1.000, macro-F1 1.000 on the last 25% of the series.

recommendations.finding: Loud Cover has a single value and therefore zero predictive power.
recommendations.action: Drop it before modelling (done implicitly by the ColumnTransformer, but it should also be removed from the stored features).
Decide explicitly: either impute with the most frequent value or keep a dedicated 'Unknown' class. Do not drop rows here: they carry valid temperature/visibility data.
Use class_weight='balanced' (already configured) and report balanced accuracy / macro-F1 instead of raw accuracy, which is dominated by 'rain'.
Drop them before cross-validation unless they are genuine repeated readings; otherwise the same hour is scored twice and scores become optimistic.

recommendations.finding: 2 feature(s) flagged as noisy: Wind Speed (km/h), Visibility (km).
recommendations.action: Prefer robust scaling or tree models; if the noise is sensor jitter, aggregate hourly readings or apply a short rolling median before training.

recommendations.finding: 1,288 reading(s) outside the physical range were masked.
recommendations.action: Add the same range checks to the ingestion step and log/reject abnormal readings instead of silently storing them (e.g. Pressure = 0 mb during a storm).

recommendations.finding: 6,424 IQR outlier reading(s); extremes are usually real weather events.
recommendations.action: Do not delete them blindly: check that they correspond to storms/heatwaves, then use robust metrics (balanced accuracy / F1) and tree models rather than winsorising.

recommendations.finding: 'Temperature (C)' and 'Apparent Temperature (C)' are almost the same signal (r=0.99).
recommendations.action: Keep one of the pair or combine them; otherwise importance is split between two identical columns and multicollinearity makes coefficients unstable.

recommendations.finding: 'Temperature (C)' is the strongest impurity driver; permutation top is 'Temperature (C)'.
recommendations.action: Retain the top drivers but confirm they are available at prediction time; drop features whose permutation importance is near zero.
